metaDescription: Combine UNESCO Xanthos, Patara ruins and dunes, and Saklıkent Gorge in one day: canyon footwear, Caretta caretta sunset closures, and Kaş vs Fethiye.
quickAnswer: Combine UNESCO-listed Xanthos, Saklıkent Gorge, and Patara ruins and dunes in one self-driven loop by visiting Xanthos early before heat builds, cooling off in Saklıkent's icy canyon at midday, and finishing at Patara by mid-afternoon before the summer Caretta caretta sunset closure. Wear strapped water shoes in the gorge; both Kaş and Fethiye work as bases.

body.text: How do you combine Patara ruins, dunes and Saklıkent Gorge in one day?

Start at 08:30 with the exposed limestone ruins of Xanthos (and optionally nearby Letoon, 4 kilometers away) while morning shade still helps, drive 25 minutes inland to wade through shaded Saklıkent Gorge during peak midday heat, and finish at Patara Ancient City, the sand dunes, and Patara Beach from 15:00 until closing.

Inscribed on the [UNESCO World Heritage List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/484) in 1988, [Xanthos and Letoon](https://turkishmuseums.com/blog/detail/turkiyes-unesco-sites-lycia-s-shining-cities-xanthos-letoon/10022/4) were Lycia's capital and federal sanctuary, noted for pillar tombs and a trilingual inscription ([Turkish Airlines guide](https://blog.turkishairlines.com/en/xanthos-and-letoon-travel-guide/)). Saklıkent lies 25 minutes north, and [driving Saklıkent to Patara](https://www.rome2rio.com/s/Patara-Lycia/Sakl%C4%B1kent-National-Park) takes 35 minutes (30.2 km).

items: 08:30–10:00: Walk Xanthos's Roman theater, Harpy Tomb, and Lycian acropolis before tour buses arrive.
10:30–13:30: Enter Saklıkent National Park, cross the wooden boardwalk, wade upstream into the shaded canyon, and eat trout or gözleme at a riverside platform.

14:30–18:30: Tour Patara's restored [Lycian League Parliament Building](https://goturkiye.com/patara/see) and main colonnaded street, then swim at Patara Beach and walk the dunes before evening gate closure.

body.text: What footwear do you need inside Saklıkent Canyon?

You need closed-toe neoprene water shoes or securely strapped sport sandals (such as Teva or Keen styles) with grippy rubber soles. Never wear loose flip-flops, slides, or smooth-soled sneakers inside the canyon: the fast-moving river crossing at the end of the wooden boardwalk rips unsecured sandals off your feet and turns wet limestone boulders slick.

A national park since 1996, the 18-kilometer gorge rises 300 meters high and narrows to 2–4 meters, with 2–4 kilometers walkable from April to October ([Fethiye Tours](https://www.fethiyetours.com/best-of-fethiye/saklikent-gorge/), [Turquoise Collection](https://www.theturquoisecollection.com/saklikent-gorge/)). Regular shoes work on the dry boardwalk, while river wading requires strapped water shoes (or entrance rentals) plus a dry bag.
Why is Patara closed after sunset in summer?

Patara Beach closes to all visitors at dusk—typically at 19:00 or 20:00 from 15 May to 15 September—to protect nesting endangered loggerhead sea turtles (Caretta caretta). Female turtles haul ashore in darkness to dig nests in the fine sand, and artificial lights, footsteps, beach chairs, or overnight camping disrupt egg-laying and disorient hatchlings heading toward the sea.

As [2026 Patara Beach visitor rules](https://canvilia.com/en/blog/patara-beach-guide) and [Antalya coastal guides](https://antalyatouristinformation.com/d/things-to-do/beach/patara/) explain, daytime beach hours run 08:00 to 19:00 during core nesting season (extending toward 20:00 on the shoulder), umbrellas are prohibited inside marked nesting zones, and dogs, fires, and overnight stays are strictly banned. If you want golden-hour views over the dunes without breaking conservation rules, head to the elevated sand-dune ridge outside the restricted shore strip well before gate closure—and never walk onto the beach after dark. For another protected turtle coast further east, read our [Çıralı & Olympos guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/cirali-olympos-guide).
Is it better done from Kaş or Fethiye?

Both bases work comfortably by rental car or private driver, though Kaş (and especially Kalkan) puts you noticeably closer to Patara and Xanthos, while Fethiye sits closer to Saklıkent Gorge. If you rely on public transport rather than a car, Fethiye is easier for Saklıkent alone, whereas Kaş works better for Patara and Kaputaş.

faq.q: Does one ticket cover both Patara Ancient City and Patara Beach?
faq.a: Yes. Passing through the archaeological site gate gives you access to both the Lycian ruins and Patara Beach. Museum Pass Türkiye is accepted at the archaeological checkpoint, and multi-entry beach cards are sold locally for repeat visits.

faq.q: Is Saklıkent Gorge open for river walking in winter or early spring?
faq.a: The wooden boardwalk usually stays open year-round, but heavy winter rains and spring snowmelt raise water levels and currents too high for safe river wading. Canyon wading typically opens from April or May through October.

faq.q: Can you visit both Xanthos and Letoon in the same morning?
faq.a: Yes. Xanthos and Letoon sit just 4 kilometers apart near Kınık and share the same UNESCO World Heritage listing. Budget about 60–75 minutes for Xanthos and 35–45 minutes for Letoon's three temples.

faq.q: How long do you need inside Saklıkent Gorge?
faq.a: Plan 1 hour if you only walk the dry wooden boardwalk to the river springs, or 2 to 3 hours if you wade upstream through the narrow limestone canyon and pause for lunch by the water.

faq.q: Can you watch the sunset on Patara Beach in July or August?
faq.a: No. During core Caretta caretta nesting season (15 May to 15 September), the beach closes between 19:00 and 20:00 before full dark to keep nesting turtles undisturbed.

faq.q: Are there lockers or changing rooms at Saklıkent Gorge?
faq.a: Yes, simple changing stalls and small paid lockers are available near the canyon entrance cafes, though leaving valuables locked out of sight in your car trunk is simpler.
